pullRequests.author: Veradictus
pullRequests.head: main
pullRequests.body:
Step one of aligning this repository with the NTSC decomp, towards an eventual merge: its names, its newer header changes, and a build fix for the bumped submodule. Nothing moves between files and no compiled byte changes.

pullRequests.title: refactor: write 43 functions with the NTSC decomp's structs
pullRequests.author: Veradictus
pullRequests.head: main
pullRequests.body:
Rewrites the bodies of 43 matched functions (19 in the executable, 24 in shared and level overlays) with the NTSC decomp's structs, enums, field and local names in place of raw offsets and casts (748 raw-offset spots in the originals of the batch, 205 left). Types our headers do not have yet are defined next to the functions that use them, for a later header import.

pullRequests.title: Match PAL v2 startup and animation; repair overlay identities
pullRequests.author: llesieur99
pullRequests.head: codex/rac1-finish-20261023
pullRequests.body:
This PAL v2 (SCES_509.16) change completes nine C functions and repairs overlay boundaries that previously split complete functions or conflated different callees.
The C additions cover the sound-system startup, MPEG DMA submission, CRT exit, four menu/moby helpers, and the animation update with its distinct mapping-reset helper. The sound object uses the original ps2eeas assembler as a whole; compiler-generated scalar constants are placed with explicit, checked linker metadata. No compiler…

pullRequests.title: refactor(names): eleven Blarg Station functions, identified in game
pullRequests.author: cnobis
pullRequests.head: feat/names-blarg
pullRequests.body:
Names for eleven Blarg Station functions. I found each object by playing the native port with the F3 moby inspector open. The inspector lists each nearby moby's class and update function, and "labels in the picture" puts the class number on the object itself. The names go through config/names_local.tsv, so they are macros and the build stays byte-identical.

pullRequests.title: docs(permuter): point to OpenRAC's shared permuter tool
pullRequests.author: Veradictus
pullRequests.head: main
pullRequests.body: Adds a note at the top of docs/PERMUTER.md: OpenRAC's tools/permuter runs decomp-permuter for every Ratchet & Clank decomp with one engine. Its rac1/pal profile compiles each candidate through tools/permuter_compile.py in the build image and counts a score 0 only when tools/try_func.py says EXACT. The setup in this repo is unchanged.
